title: AMD set to lease planned 5C data center in Pennsylvania
html:
A large-scale data center campus is being planned in Pennsylvania, with chip firm AMD earmarked as the end-user.

First reported by News-Item, AMD has been identified as the intended tenant of a proposed data center in Mount Carmel Township in Northumberland County.

The development, located along Arcos Drive and known as Project Phoenix, is the subject of a conditional use application submitted by Fit Energy USA Inc. for approximately 351 acres of former mining property north of Route 61 and west of Route 54, near Kulpmont and Marion Heights.

Natural gas generation firm Fit Energy acquired the property from Susquehanna Coal Company in April this year.

Application documents on Mount Carmel’s website suggest data center firm 5C is the intended operator of the campus. 5C PHL01 Inc. is negotiating an agreement to purchase the undeveloped property from Fit Energy. AMD is listed as the intended end user.

An open house event around the project took place in July. The first single-story building could total 160MW of IT capacity across 482,895 sq ft (44,862 sqm).

The first overall phase could see two buildings developed totaling 1.5 million sq ft (139,354 sqm), with four more totaling 1.85 million sq ft (171,870 sqm) developed last, alongside on-site generation.

According to a dedicated project website, primary power on the site will come from fuel cells. The liquid-cooled campus will reportedly use closed-loop cooling to reduce water use, along with air-cooled chillers.

Hypertec formed 5C Group last year when its Hypertec Cloud division was spun out and merged with the acquired 5C Data Centers.

The Canadian firm has facilities in development across Ohio, Arizona, North Carolina, and Tennessee that could reach more than 2GW at full build-out. Expansion into Europe is also planned to support AI firm Together AI.

5C and AMD announced a “strategic collaboration” in July to “accelerate the development of the next generation gigascale AI campuses,” though few details were provided.

In October, Fit Energy announced plans for a Pennsylvania natural-gas-powered fuel cell generation and data center project in Newport Township, Luzerne County. The project is set to be developed on former mining and quarry land. Fit is working with FuelCell Energy, Inc. on the project, known as the Newport Township Data Center.

Chip designer AMD, which is competing with Nvidia to supply GPUs fueling the AI boom, is set to lease gigawatts of capacity across the US from Core Scientific. AMD is also set to lease 50MW of capacity from Riot in Texas.
summary: 5C looking to buy site in Mount Carmel from FIT Energy
